correctness.rationale: Complete infinite-family proof: all-horizon monotonicity follows from mandatory passage through the preceding level, and finite-horizon Bellman recursion selects the parent; the depth chain is then exact. The first-passage continued fraction and mean difference recurrence are algebraic identities. Binary-tree CLT couples the reflected walk below an unreflected inward-biased walk with a uniformly bounded mean gap of at most 40. Higher-branching exponential law follows from leaf regeneration, exact gambler ruin success probability, uniform cycle second moments, and a renewal Laplace transform. Standalone verify.py gave 2,538 exact Bellman-state/PGF checks and numerical finite-state mean comparisons. No finite test is used as a proof of h-to-infinity convergence.

originality.rationale: The full pertinent 2019 choice-walk article already identifies the 5/9 inward probability at degree three and outward bias on a four-regular infinite tree; neither qualitative observation is claimed. The assessed result goes beyond both by proving a common policy optimizes every deadline on finite b-ary trees, determining the complete finite-depth first-passage generating function, and deriving Gaussian versus exponential normalized limit laws with exact constants. Zhang (2019) supplies general first-passage moment identities, limiting novelty of the mean alone, but does not state the controlled-walk fluctuation classification. Targeted public-literature negative searches supply only best-knowledge corroboration, not a uniqueness certificate.

value.rationale: The exact optimal controlled-tree hitting law, including the rational full finite-height distribution and an infinite-family Gaussian-to-exponential fluctuation transition at the smallest branching change, is a motivated quantitative completion of the source paper’s qualitative subcubic-versus-higher-degree observation. It identifies both mean scaling (linear versus exponential in height) and uncertainty shape (concentrated versus memoryless), and gives a precise benchmark for graph-based stochastic control. These are not arbitrary small-parameter numerical constants or a simple re-expression of an existing table; the model is canonical and the result covers all fixed integer branching factors b>=2.
